summary: Oxford County, ME lookout tower in Batchelder's Grant, dated 1940 and removed in the 1940s; the FFLA list marks it gone and no source read describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Removed in the 1940s according to the Sun Journal table; no source read describes the site now or whether it is open to visitors

events.note: Sun Journal table gives 1940 as the tower's date; the table does not label the date, so this may be the install year

evidence.supports: Roost (The Roost) is listed among the Oxford County towers
the table counts twelve towers in Oxford County
FFLA lists the Roost as in Oxford County with its tower gone

sources.title: Maine fire towers: By the numbers

notes_for_editor: Two short sources only, so the story is thin and the confidence is low. The FFLA Maine chapter state listing table (last update 12/30/2021; page URL not identified, so not cited) gives Roost (The Roost), Batchelders Grant, Oxford, elevation 1300 ft, a wooden tower installed 1940, and removed in the 1940s. A Maine chapter Facebook photo (https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=721881040659090) appeared only in a search snippet, describing a Roost on a high spot in the White Mountain National Forest just off Route 113 as a federal Forest Service site. The page could not be read, so nothing from it is quoted or used; it may describe a different Roost. A human should confirm which site it is before anything from it is added to this record.
